questions.question: Explain the concept of intersectionality with an example. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the concept of intersectionality with an example.
  • a. Intersectionality refers to how different aspects of a person’s identity—such as
  • gender, caste, class, race, and sexuality—interact to shape their experiences
  • of privilege or oppression.
  • b. It recognizes that people face multiple, overlapping forms of discrimination in
  • society.
  • c. This concept helps in understanding social inequality more deeply rather than
  • viewing each identity in isolation.
  • d. Policies and social actions using intersectionality aim to address these
  • combined disadvantages.
  • e. Example: A Dalit woman may face both caste-based and gender-based
  • discrimination, unlike an upper-caste woman or a Dalit man
  • [U]/[CO1]

questions.question: Compare and contrast the development of a planned city versus an unplanned city. / [CO3] [5x4 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• .
  • Compare and contrast the development of a planned city versus an unplanned city.
  • a. Planned cities are developed systematically with zoning, infrastructure, and
  • services designed in advance (e.g., Chandigarh).
  • b. Unplanned cities grow spontaneously without proper layout or urban planning
  • (e.g., many old city areas).
  • c. Planned cities offer better sanitation, transport, and green spaces.
  • d. Unplanned cities often face overcrowding, pollution, and inadequate public
  • services.
  • e. • Proper urban planning in cities promotes sustainability, efficiency, and a better
  • quality of life.
  • [An]/
  • [CO3]

questions.question: Critique the effectiveness of existing environmental laws in protecting vulnerable communities in India. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• .
  • Critique the effectiveness of existing environmental laws in protecting vulnerable
  • communities in India.
  • a. India has major environmental laws like the Environment Protection Act
  • (1986), Air Act (1981), and Water Act (1974).
  • b. While these laws aim to prevent pollution and ensure ecological balance, their
  • implementation remains weak.
  • c. Industrial and developmental projects often ignore the consent and rights of local
  • and tribal populations.
  • d. Lack of proper monitoring and corruption undermine enforcement of
  • environmental regulations.
  • e. Judicial interventions (like NGT rulings) help but are limited by slow processes
  • and poor compliance.
  • f. Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA) are often manipulated to favor
  • corporate interests.
  • g. Vulnerable communities suffer disproportionately from pollution, displacement,
  • and resource loss.
  • h. Policies rarely integrate climate justice or protection for marginalized
  • livelihoods (farmers, fishers, Adivasis).
  • i. Strengthening local governance, transparency, and public participation is
  • essential.
  • j. Hence, while laws exist, their ineffective implementation fails to adequately
  • protect vulnerable groups.
  • [E]/[CO3

questions.question: Discuss the role of social movements in addressing social problems with examples. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• .
  • Discuss the role of social movements in addressing social problems with examples.
  • a. Social movements are collective efforts by people to demand justice, equality, and
  • policy change.
  • b. They challenge social norms, institutions, and power structures that perpetuate
  • inequality.
  • c. Movements like the Dalit Movement fought caste discrimination and
  • untouchability.
  • d. The Women’s Movement in India addressed issues of gender bias, violence, and
  • equal rights.
  • e. Environmental movements such as the Chipko Movement and Narmada
  • Bachao Andolan protested ecological exploitation.
  • f. The LGBTQ+ rights movement pushed for decriminalizing homosexuality (Sec.
  • 377 judgment).
  • g. Youth and student movements have influenced education reforms and democratic
  • participation.
  • h. Social movements provide platforms for marginalized voices and grassroots
  • leadership.
  • i. They also influence public opinion, media discourse, and legislative reforms.
  • j. Thus, social movements act as vital instruments of democratic participation and
  • social transformation.
  • [An]/
  • [CO4]

questions.question: Discuss the application of conflict theory in addressing caste, class, or gender inequality. / [CO1] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• .
  • Discuss the application of conflict theory in addressing caste, class, or gender
  • inequality
  • a. Conflict theory, proposed by Karl Marx, views society as divided by power and
  • resource inequalities.
  • b. It argues that social change occurs through struggles between dominant and
  • oppressed groups.
  • c. In caste inequality, conflict theory explains how upper castes maintain
  • dominance through control over land and culture.
  • d. Dalit movements and affirmative action challenge this structural oppression.
  • e. In class inequality, it highlights the exploitation of workers by capitalist elites
  • who control production.
  • f. Trade unions and socialist movements embody resistance to class-based
  • exploitation.
  • [An]/
  • [CO1]
